title: Purity of an irreducible lisse constituent on a smooth affine base
statement: Let $k_0$ be a finite field, let $\ell$ be a prime distinct from its characteristic, and let $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\to\mathbf C$ be a field embedding [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k_0$-scheme. Let $G$ be a lisse constructible Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex; def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], real in the sense of [def-wf-iota-real]. Let $i:G_1\hookrightarrow G_2$ and $j:G_2\hookrightarrow G$ be monomorphisms of lisse Weil sheaves, and suppose $V=\operatorname{coker}(i)$ is nonzero and has no nonzero proper lisse Weil subobject. Then there exists a real number $w$ such that $V$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ at every closed point of $X_0$. The Lean specialization uses the source-library constructible pro-etale Weil category and its matching local Frobenius and purity predicates; no connectedness or positive-dimension hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--5, applied to one irreducible subquotient; paragraph 7 for dimension zero.

proof.text: Nonzeroness of the irreducible quotient gives a nonzero stalk at a closed point, using the proved source theorem WeilSheaf.exists_nontrivial_stalk_of_not_isZero. Apply Module.End.exists_eigenvalue to that finite-dimensional stalk and fix one anchor eigenvalue alpha. Define w=2 log|iota(alpha)|/log(q_x).

For any closed y and any eigenvalue beta at y, apply the simultaneous geometric curve test to alpha,beta. Its real ambient lisse sheaf H and irreducible lisse cokernel satisfy the hypotheses of the proved curve purity theorem. Thus alpha^e at s and beta^f at t have one curve weight v, with q_s=q_x^e and q_t=q_y^f.

Since e,f are positive, log|iota(alpha^e)|=e log|iota(alpha)| and log(q_x^e)=e log(q_x) show that normalized weight is unchanged by matching positive powers. The same computation for beta proves its normalized weight equals w. The residue cardinalities exceed one and Frobenius eigenvalues are nonzero, so normalized weight w is equivalent to |iota(beta)|=q_y^(w/2). This gives punctual purity at every y, including zero stalks vacuously.

theorem IsReal.exists_isPunctuallyPureOfWeight_cokernel_of_smooth_affine
    {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime]
    [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [IsAffine X]
    [Smooth (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    {ι : PadicAlgCl l →+* ℂ} {G : WeilSheaf k₀ l X}
    (hG : G.IsLisse) (hreal : G.IsReal ι) {G₁ G₂ : WeilSheaf k₀ l X}
    (i : G₁ ⟶ G₂) (j : G₂ ⟶ G) [Mono i] [Mono j]
    (h₁ : G₁.IsLisse) (h₂ : G₂.IsLisse)
    (hirr : (cokernel i).IsIrreducibleLisse) :
    ∃ w : ℝ, (cokernel i).IsPunctuallyPureOfWeight ι w
